newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends easy, gilts quiet in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends easy, gilts quiet in dull trade.

text.p: Indian call money ended Wednesday at 4.75-5.0 percent, marginally down from opening quotes of 5.0-5.25 percent, dealers said.
They said call money opened higher on fears of liquidity tightening due to funds outflows but eased during the day.
The Reserve Bank of India accepted bids for 33 billion rupees at a repo auction on Tuesday. It holds an auction of federal government bonds worth 30 billion rupees later on Wednesday.

"There were some fears initially that liquidity will tighten on account of outflows towards the two auctions," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "But as the day wore on, it became clear that funds were available and rates came down."
He said market players expected call money to be in a 5.0-5.5 percent range on Thursday.
Dealers said trade in government securities was dull as market players awaited the three-year bond auction results.
"We are waiting for the cut-off yield at the bond auction," said a dealer. "It will enable us to take a view on short- and medium-term interest rates. Fresh positions will be taken only after that."
He said prices of government securities were largely steady in light trade, with prices moving only a few paise.

"Most of the trade was in treasury bills with deals of about 600 million rupees in the bill maturing in April 1998 alone," he said. "It was traded at a yield of 9.5 percent. Otherwise, there was hardly any trade."
